title: Output Contract Watchtower: regression harness for graceful-degrade and constrained-decode alarms
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an end-to-end regression harness and operational playbook ("Watchtower") that continuously validates JSON-mode enforcement and constrained-decoding behavior across streaming, tool-calls, and model-compatibility changes. The Watchtower should detect schema drift, measure graceful-degradation behavior when strict decoding fails, surface actionable alarms, and verify fallback policies (permissive schema, sentinel insertion, or model-variant routing). This ticket covers test design, harness implementation, instrumentation, and Console dashboard integration.
acceptance_criteria: A continuous test harness executes nightly against a matrix of model variants and streaming configurations and reports pass/fail per test case.
The system detects and records partial-stream JSON malformations and classifies them as: transient-stream-noise, decoder-rejection, or schema-mismatch with >=90% precision on seeded cases.

When constrained-decoder rejects a response, the Watchtower verifies configured fallback behavior within SLO: either permissive-unwrapped-response OR model-variant fallback OR tool-call-safe-sentinel is executed within 500ms of detection.
Generated alarms are integrated into Console as a per-model/per-route time-series and include the failing prompt id, sample output, and suggested rollback label.

Regression suite covers at least 18 scenarios including interleaved toolcall tokens, truncated KV-cache resumes, and token-gating under heavy batching. All scenarios must pass in the nightly run before release cut.
test_plan: Golden prompt set: curated 120 prompts representative of customer workloads (chat, structured forms, table extraction).
Streaming partial recovery: feed truncated and rejoined response streams with intentionally inserted noise tokens to validate reassembly heuristics.
Toolcall interleaving: simulate tool return objects inside stream and assert JSON-mode gating doesn't misattribute tokens to schema fields.
Constrained decode stress: run constrained decoders under token-gating/backpressure and verify fallback policy triggers and latency bounds.
Cross-model compatibility: run tests across three quantization and kernel-selection profiles to surface policy mismatches and decoder regressions.
Fuzzing harness: mutate golden outputs and ensure classifier can distinguish true schema drift from benign lexical variance.
steps: 1) Define canonical schema set and golden prompt set; store as versioned artifacts in the test repo.
2) Implement streaming injector that can replay HA/partial streams and interleaved toolcall payloads against runtime endpoints.
3) Add instrumentation to runtime that emits constraint-failure events and payload snapshots to the Watchtower ingestion topic.
4) Build nightly runner that executes the matrix, aggregates metrics, and writes results to the Console test dashboard.
5) Create alarm rules (threshold + anomaly) and wire to PagerDuty + internal Slack channel with automatic sample attach and rollback suggestion.
6) Run initial golden-run and iterate on false positives for two cycles; document heuristics in the playbook.
notes: Design decision: prefer graceful degradation (emit object with "__warning" field and partial data) over hard failures for most customer routes to reduce P0 incidents.

Trade-off: strict blacklist of tokens in constrained-decoder reduces hallucinated schema fields but increases false positives under noisy streaming — mitigations include adaptive thresholding and per-workload calibration.
Instrumenting full payloads raises privacy concerns; we will redact PII via a deterministic scrubber before persisting to the Watchtower topic.
We should reuse the existing schema-diff library from the validation team and extend it with a streaming-aware comparator (lineage + offsets).
timeline: 2026-03-12: streaming injector MVP and initial metrics emission
2026-03-19: constrained-decoder scenarios added and first nightly run
regressions: Previously observed: decoder rejecting valid toolcall returns when tool payloads contained nested braces (manifested as schema-mismatch).
Previously observed: partial-stream reassembly produced duplicate keys in output after a kernel scheduling change under high batching pressure.
Previously observed: fallback to permissive schema exposed a downstream consumer bug that assumed strict typing — Watchtower will surface these cross-stack regressions.
